datasets.name: Landslide inventory of the 2018 Anchorage, Alaska earthquake
datasets.verbatim: The landslide inventory used in our analysis is provided by Martinez et al. (2021).

datasets.name: Field observation data (1,301 geotagged photos)
datasets.verbatim: For this study, we used the 1,301 geotagged photos from the ground and helicopter reconnaissance collected by Grant et al. (2020a)... Field observation data can be found in Grant et al. (2020a).

datasets.name: High-resolution optical satellite imagery (WorldView-2, WorldView-3, GeoEye-1)
datasets.source: MAXAR Global Enhanced GEOINT Delivery (G-EGD) system
datasets.verbatim: High-resolution satellite imagery was downloaded using the MAXAR Global Enhanced GEOINT Delivery (G-EGD) system.

datasets.name: 1-m pre- and post-earthquake DEMs derived from lidar data
datasets.source: Alaska Division of Geological and Geophysical Surveys (DGGS)
datasets.verbatim: This study uses 1-m pre- and post-earthquake DEMs derived from lidar data acquired by the state of Alaska and made available via the Alaska Division of Geological and Geophysical Surveys (DGGS) elevation portal (DGGS Staff, 2013)... Available at: https://maps.dggs.alaska.gov/elevationdata/ (Accessed June 1, 2020).

datasets.name: Sentinel-2 multispectral satellite imagery
datasets.verbatim: The summer composites were produced using Google Earth Engine (Gorelick et al., 2017) using satellite imagery from the European Space Agency’s Sentinel-2 multispectral satellite.

datasets.name: Sentinel-1 and ALOS-2 SAR imagery
datasets.verbatim: Three sets of images are used for change detection before and after the earthquake from the Sentinel-1 and ALOS-2 satellites (Supplementary Table S1).

methods.name: SAR amplitude change detection (ACD) time series mapping
methods.summary: A workflow implemented in Google Earth Engine that generates pre- and post-event time series maps using Sentinel-1 ground range detected (GRD) products, which are processed to remove thermal noise, radiometrically and terrain calibrated, and differenced in dB units.
methods.verbatim: The Google Earth Engine code used to create the synthetic aperture radar (SAR) amplitude change detection (ACD) time series maps can be accessed via GitHub at the following link: https://github.com/MongHanHuang/GEE_SAR_landslide_detection(https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.4060268).

availability.author_statement: Full availability statement, with shared links.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are referenced or linked, with public access provided for the DEMs and other datasets via established portals. The custom Google Earth Engine code is available via a persistent GitHub repository and Zenodo archive.
